question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt this hybrid public contract, where root-level identity remains an implicit default account and named accounts inherit shared root settings?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and follows existing multi-account helpers, but accepting two public configuration shapes plus inheritance and setup-promotion behavior is a compatibility and product-contract choice that automation cannot safely make.

options.title: Approve hybrid contract
options.body: Accept root-level single-bot configuration as the implicit default account while adding named accounts and shared-root inheritance, then require a clean rebase and exact-head validation.

options.title: Require accounts-only canonical shape
options.body: Move all identities under `accounts`, add a doctor migration for shipped root-level configuration, and keep runtime/config writing on one canonical shape.

options.title: Pause multi-account support
options.body: Close or defer the PR if maintainers do not want Microsoft Teams to expose multiple bot identities in one gateway.

recommendation.title: Approve hybrid contract
recommendation.body: Accept root-level single-bot configuration as the implicit default account while adding named accounts and shared-root inheritance, then require a clean rebase and exact-head validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Main history shows the broadest ownership of the Teams channel architecture, config schema, plugin seams, and compatibility policy touched by this decision.
